name: Barbados Tridents
profile_lede: A twice-crowned founding franchise returning to the Tridents name and Barbados colours for a home-heavy finish at Kensington Oval.
history: Barbados were one of the six founding CPL franchises in 2013 and won championships under the Tridents name in 2014 and 2019. Those two titles remain part of the same Barbados franchise record.

After competing as Barbados Royals from 2021 to 2025, the team officially restored the Tridents identity for 2026. The ownership and management structure remains with Royals Sports Group while the playing name and colours reconnect with Barbados.
The 2026 campaign has a powerful home conclusion: five Barbados league matches are scheduled at Kensington Oval before the venue stages the Eliminator, both Qualifiers and the final.

profile_highlights.label: Honours
profile_highlights.title: Two-time champions
profile_highlights.text: The Tridents lifted the CPL trophy in 2014 and again in 2019.

profile_highlights.label: Identity
profile_highlights.title: The name is back
profile_highlights.text: Barbados return to the Tridents name and national colours after five seasons as the Royals.

profile_highlights.label: Home finish
profile_highlights.title: Kensington takes centre stage
profile_highlights.text: Five home league matches and the complete playoff series are scheduled in Bridgetown.

summary: Barbados return to the Tridents identity and national colours in 2026, with Gudakesh Motie, Sherfane Rutherford and Brandon King among the senior Caribbean core.
storyline: Kensington Oval stages five Barbados league matches and then all four playoff games, giving the franchise a home finish to the regular season.
